svg.text: A system diagram shows where signals enter, how they are conditioned
and where the results are used. Labelled connections describe interfaces;
physical and software behaviour need separate evidence.
Follow each signal from source to destination. Mark the reference,
expected voltage range, loading and useful test points. Explain how you
Draw and annotate source, processing, transmitter, channel and receiver
blocks. Identify which interfaces carry electrical signals. This is a
block-diagram teaching exercise, not an end-to-end communication
This is a connection-planning drawing. Follow each labelled net, identify
the real terminals and add your bench measurements. No simulation is
The buffer represents a processing stage; choose suitable analogue
conditioning for a real sensor. Follow SENSOR → CONDITIONED → TX
→ RX → RECEIVED. The final physical output is a system label.
Use an equation, a truth table or a state sequence to justify your
prediction. Include units and discuss the model assumptions.
Check the physical layout with your teacher before construction.
